header.description: Two-ship SAME-AIRFRAME altitude-contrast scenario for B5 (ISA atmosphere, v1.21r0), RE-MEASURED at v1.22r0 (supercharger critical altitude): two Spitfire Mk Vs fly the IDENTICAL 4-phase schedule with altitude as the ONLY independent variable — AC0 low (800 m, below the Merlin 45's crit_alt_m 6000 -> lapse 1, rated power, sigma drag ~0.92) vs AC1 high (6900 m, ABOVE the critical altitude -> lapse = sigma(6900)/sigma(6000) ~0.90, sigma drag ~0.49). They can never interact (no fire phases -> no projectiles exist; started on opposite great-circle arcs, lon 0 psi 90 vs lon 90 psi 270). Schedule: phase 0 (t=0) full-throttle 1 g wings-level acceleration from TAS 120 — by t=2000 the low ship reaches ~131.5 m/s while the high ship reaches ~138.4: under the supercharger the HIGH ship is now the FASTER one in TAS (near-rated power up to just past the critical altitude, half the drag) — the historically correct shape the v1.22r0 lapse pins, and the REVERSAL of the B5 divergence (which had thrust falling with raw sigma, low ship faster by ~11 m/s); phase 1 (t=2000) a 1 s g 6.0 pull — the LOW ship has aero headroom (n_aero stays ~[9.41,10.00] > 6, the commanded 6 g is delivered un-clamped, below n_max_struct 8), the HIGH ship is AERO-LIMITED (n_aero ~[5.44,5.83] < 6 — the SAME command is clamped to the B3 C_Lmax ceiling, which B5 made altitude-dependent); phase 2 (t=2100) floats at g 0.5 while the zoom tops out; phase 3 (t=2400) recovers to 1 g at throttle 0.8. The low ship climbs ~800->1134 m CROSSING the 1000 m sigma-LUT node; the high ship climbs ~6900->7209 m CROSSING the 7000 m node — both ships traverse a sigma LUT segment boundary in flight, so the 17-node table's interpolation AND segment switching are pinned in the golden bytes (not just single-segment evaluation). No guns: hp/regions full, ammo untouched, kills 0, last_hit_by -1 — this golden pins the B5/v1.22r0 FLIGHT-MODEL coupling (sigma -> thrust lapse/drag/n_aero) in C++ <-> Python lockstep; combat goldens own the weapon arcs. Exercises: air_sigma LUT interpolation in two different segments + two node crossings, the supercharger thrust lapse on BOTH sides of a critical altitude (rated below, sigma/sigma_crit above), sigma-scaled dynamic pressure (divergent drag), and the altitude-dependent B3 aero ceiling (one clamped pull, one un-clamped pull, same command).
header.introduced: NEW golden for B5 (ISA atmosphere, seal v1.21r0): the first scenario in which ALTITUDE is the only independent variable — it pins the sigma(alt) density-ratio LUT end-to-end through the flight model in C++ <-> Python lockstep. RE-MEASURED at v1.22r0 (schedule unchanged): the supercharger lapse REVERSES the acceleration divergence — the high ship is now the faster one, exactly the effect the critical-altitude model exists to produce. See ADR-Step8-FlightModel-Supercharger-v1.22r0.
